literal: They would renounce indeed, those who lack enjoyments, if things destined to happen would pass away without making them experience.
translation: Those who lack the means of enjoyment would surely renounce the world, if only destined events would pass away without forcing them to experience their fruits.
modern: அனுபவிக்க வேண்டிய விதிப்பயன்கள் தங்களை அனுபவிக்கச் செய்யாமல் சும்மா கடந்து போய்விடுமானால், நுகர்பொருள்கள் இல்லாத ஏழைகள் உலகத்தைத் துறந்து துறவிகளாகிவிடுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the inescapable power of destiny. The poet suggests that those who suffer from a lack of basic resources and enjoyments ('tuppuravu illār') would easily renounce worldly life ('tuṟappār') to escape their misery. However, they are unable to do so because destiny ('uṟaṟpāla') does not pass away ('kaḻiyum') without forcing them to experience ('ūṭṭā') the fruits of their past actions. Thus, even the desire to renounce is governed and restricted by destiny, binding individuals to their destined experiences.
